programme.title: Saschiz Old Town, Romania
programme.desc: Saschiz, village, and commune, Mureș județ county is located in central Romania. The villages of Saschiz, Mihai Viteazu, and Cloașterf make up the larger commune of Saschiz. Located in the old region of Transylvania, it lies about 20 km east of Sighișoara"&". First documented in the 14th century, Saschiz is known for its medieval fortress and church constructed by Transylvanian Saxons, a German speaker. They settled in Transylvania when it was part of Hungary. The ruins of the 14th-century fortress sit atop "&"a hill overlooking the village. The late 15th-century fortified church has Gothic details and an imposing clock tower. Along with five other villages with fortified churches, Saschiz was inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage sites in 1999.

programme.title: Beelzebub [English Dub]
programme.desc: Oga Tatsumi is a crazy-strong, ruthless high school delinquent who's nicknamed the "Rampaging Ogre". One day, while dunking some punk, he rescues a big guy who comes ~floating~ down the river. When he does, the big guy splits in half and out pops a bouncing baby boy! But this baby is actually Kaiser de Emperana Beelzebub IV (Baby Beel), the son of the Great Demon Lord, and he came from the Demon World in order to destroy humanity!

programme.title: Beelzebub [English Dub]
programme.desc: Oga has been chosen to be the parent of Beelzebub, the son of the Great Demon Lord. However Oga's suffering since every time Baby Beel cries he lets out a severe electric shock. Plus, according to Baby Beel's demon maidservant Hildegarde (Hilda), if Baby Beel moves farther than 15 meters away from his human parent Oga, the electric shock will reach lethal levels. Oga shuffles to school with Baby Beel clinging to his back, having no other choice, and begins to search for someone even stronger than him that Baby Beel will take a liking to, in order to get this monkey off his back, literally!

programme.title: Beelzebub [English Dub]
programme.desc: Oga loses the powdered milk that Hilda prepared for him, and instead buys a bunch of "Yogurty" from a vending machine for Beel. But it turns out that's the favorite drink of one of Ishiyama's Big Four, the "Ishiyama Tohoshinki"; the third year Kanzaki Hajime. Oga hears about how horrible and ruthless a guy Kanzaki is, and runs into the third year classroom to try and dump Baby Beel off on him. When he sees Kanzaki's evil looking face, Oga thinks that this just might be his chance!

programme.title: Magic Kaito 1412 [English Dub]
programme.sub-title: Magic Kaito 1412 EP13 Get Away from Him [English Dub]
programme.desc: Kaito takes a break from thieving to go on his class ski trip, but when his teacher holds a couples-only masquerade ski tournament, he finds himself in a tug-of-war between the witchy Akako and childhood friend Aoko!

programme.title: Magic Kaito 1412 [English Dub]
programme.sub-title: Magic Kaito 1412 EP14 Crystal Mother [English Dub]
programme.desc: Kaito and Aoko are on a luxury train with the Queen of Ingram, her son, and the Principality of Ingram's Crystal Mother, a huge topaz that may contain the Pandora jewel. The queen has the real jewel cleverly hidden, though, making it a challenge for Kaito/Kid to find it before the train reaches Osaka. On top of that, he's got competition, as there's a Snake on the train!

programme.title: Magic Kaito 1412 [English Dub]
programme.sub-title: Magic Kaito 1412 EP15 The Princess and the Thief's Improv [English Dub]
programme.desc: When a princess with a priceless jewel comes to town, Inspector Nakamori is sidelined by a detective from her country who shoots first and... shoots again later, until his quarry is killed. Naturally, his target is Kid the Phantom Thief!

programme.title: Demon Slayer -Kimetsu no Yaiba- The Movie: Mugen Train [English Subtitle] (2020)
programme.desc: Tanjiro and Nezuko, along with Zenitsu and Inosuke, join one of the most powerful swordsmen within the Demon Slayer Corps, Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku, to face the demon aboard the Mugen Train on track to despair.

programme.title: Sonic X (2004)
programme.desc: The President demands the search for Dr. Eggman after Sonic destroys the Egg Fort. Meanwhile, Sonic and his friends are taking a well-deserved vacation where they discover that another Chaos Emerald is nearby.

programme.title: Sonic X (2004)
programme.sub-title: EP17 The Adventures of Knuckles and Hawk
programme.desc: Knuckles rescues a man named Hawk from ancient ruins. Discovering later that Hawk had discovered a chaos emerald, Knuckles seeks for him once again in Oriental City. There he is confronted by some local thugs Li Yan and the Bruiser Boys.

programme.title: Sonic X
programme.desc: When Sonic, Tails, Chris and the Egg Fort crash land on the Nature Continent after a fight, Tails and Chris protest against a dam while Sonic is caught in a battle against Decoe, Bocoe, E-65 and Eggman.

programme.title: LUPIN THE 3rd PART 2 [English Dub] (1978)
programme.sub-title: LUPIN THE 3rd PART 2 -EP16 Crude Reproduction, Perfect Frame [English Dub]
programme.desc: Lupin is suffering from Transformation Sickness, an illness that transforms him into a cruel, cold-blooded criminal at the stroke of midnight, and leaves him with no recollection of his murderous crime spree in the morning. In despair, Lupin even contemplates taking his own life, but is the "other Lupin" really Lupin?

programme.title: LUPIN THE 3rd PART 2 [English Dub] (1978)
programme.desc: A small Arab nation has received a blackmail notice. Pay a $100 million or have their oil fields blown up. Lupin targets the money, but his plans are hindered when he finds out the culprits are using human bombs. Will the desert winds blow in Lupin's favor or will everything blow up in his face?

programme.title: LUPIN THE 3rd PART 2 [English Dub] (1978)
programme.sub-title: LUPIN THE 3rd PART 2 -EP18 My Birthday Pursuit [English Dub]
programme.desc: The Black Panther, the world's largest emerald, gets its name from the black panther that appears inside it when a light shines on the emerald at a particular angle. After capturing this one-of-a-kind emerald, Lupin hides it in a museum to retrieve it at a later time. However, the emerald goes missing and things get even more complicated when two rivaling inspectors take on the case. Will Lupin get his hands on the emerald again?

programme.title: Jungle Drums 1943
programme.desc: Superman vs. a secret Nazi outpost disguised as a jungle temple.

programme.title: I Never Changes My Altitude 1937
programme.desc: Popeye is sitting outside Olive's lunchroom at the airport, distraught. She's closed the business to fly away with an aviator (Bluto, of course). But it's hardly what she expected; he has her painting his plane, while it's flying; when she says she's rather go back to Popeye, he tries to throw her off the plane. Popeye sees this, and takes off in a plane, just in time to help her out. The boys get into a dogfight, and Bluto manages to demolish Popeye's plane. As Popeye is falling, he grabs a duck and feeds the duck spinach. The duck manages to fly him up to Bluto's plane, Popeye has some spinach of his own, and he teaches Bluto a lesson. Popeye picks up Olive and crashes the plane into the diner, opening it (and providing a new counter).

programme.title: Out to Punch 1956
programme.desc: Popeye's training for his boxing match with Bluto by jumping rope with a massive chain. Bluto, who's lazy about everything except sabotage, decides he needs to stop Popeye. He fills Popeye's heavy bag with iron junk, but Popeye punches it over the fence onto Bluto. Next, he pulls on the springs attached to the wall with a motorcycle, but Popeye pulls so hard he throws Bluto and the cycle through the building and into a well. Popeye is walking -- or actually, prancing -- behind Olive on the way to the match, so Bluto tries a bit more sabotage: first an oil slick, which slows Popeye down briefly, then some quick-dry cement in a puddle. This gives Popeye cement overshoes, and when he gets to the arena, he's exhausted. Olive stands him up, but Bluto treats him like a punching bag. He's got Popeye on the floor (under the ring), so Olive finally breaks out the spinach. Popeye knocks Bluto through the roof, right into the hospital. The photographers ask for a picture, and Popeye's biceps form the words

programme.title: Gold Rush Daze 1939
programme.desc: A man stops for gas on his way to dig for gold. The man at the station tells him what it was like back in 1849 in San Francisco, which we see. A sucker is hauled off the street and sat down at a card game; he dashes off as soon as someone shouts "they found gold in the hills" but others stake claims before he can. He ends up chopping off a cliff, falling down, and landing in the hospital. The doctor gives him news of another gold strike and he rushes out to begin panning. After some more mining gags and a song, we see a montage of more failed gold strikes. Back to the present day, where the storyteller claims to have sworn off gold, until a rider passes through with news of another strike, when he trades the station for the car and sets out after the gold.

programme.title: The Draft Horse 1942
programme.desc: A farm horse tries to enlist in the army, but despite his virtuoso display of wartime histrionics, he's rejected when he flunks the physical. Dejected, he wanders into a mock battlefield, which tells him what war is really like.

programme.title: Now Hear This 1962
programme.desc: In this very abstract cartoon, a hard-of-hearing old Britisher finds a red horn and uses it as a megaphone, unaware that it is really a lost horn from the Devil's forehead. The Britisher finds that the horn has the effect of amplifying every sound psychedelically and causing him serious bodily harm

programme.title: Campus Capers 1949

The highlights are a screwy college fight-song and a statute-of-liberty misdirection football play in which the Statute of Liberty participates.

Unfortunately, the baby swallows a balloon and floats out the window, and Felix has to find him and bring him back before the man gets home.

programme.desc: Noah gets the word: build an ark in seven days. His sons cut the necessary trees in three days, and much furious sawing and hammering follows. But there's no rest, as they need to round up all the animals. Noah boards the animals, then his sons, their wives, and his wife (who packed a ferocious picnic). The rains and flood begin. The animals soon develop cabin fever and get restless, but Mrs. Noah has the answer: "Music has charms to soothe the savage beast." His sons find instruments and begin playing; everyone dances. But Harry the hippo dances with everyone but his wife; Noah goes to her, and while she tells him not to mention Harry's name, Noah convinces her that Harry is thinking only of her. The rains end; Noah sends a dove out who brings back an olive branch. They land on Mount Ararat and disembark.

programme.title: Parlez Vous Woo 1956
programme.desc: Olive is so captived by "The International", a radio personality with a French accent, that she'd rather stay home than go out on a date with Popeye. Bluto, overhearing this, comes to the door as the character. Popeye does his best to get Olive back, to no avail. Finally, Bluto challenges Popeye to a duel, ultimately stabbing him in the chest where his can of spinach was. Popeye unmasks Bluto, then eats another can of spinach to give himself a French accent.

programme.title: Barnacle Bill 1930
programme.desc: Sailor Bimbo (as Barnacle Bill) jumps ship with his little black book and visits his lady friend, Betty Boop (with dog's ears).

programme.title: Scotty Finds a Home 1935
programme.desc: A young anthropomorphic kitten wants a pet. He happens to find a puppy with no owner and takes him in. When the Scotty tracks mud into the house, Grandma says that her grandson cannot keep him. A transient bulldog is walking by as Grandma puts a pie in the windowsill to cool. He barges into the house and terrorizes the family, demanding they feed him. Scotty rushes back to the house and saves the family, causing Grandma to decide that they can keep him after all.

programme.title: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River
programme.desc: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River is a documentary focusing on the World Heritage sites and cultural–ecological conservation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Through the lens of Ningxia’s heritage stories, the film highlights China’s commitment to World Heritage preservation, ecological restoration, and cultural continuity — presenting to global audiences a land where history and modernity intertwine, and where desert and oasis coexist. By following the guardians of the Western Xia Imperial Tombs, desert restorers in the Tengger Desert, Great Wall rangers at Sanguankou, traditional sheepskin raft craftsmen, and managers of the Yellow River irrigation system in Qingtongxia, the program reveals Ningxia’s distinctive contributions to cultural heritage, natural ecology, and intangible traditions — and the enduring human spirit behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise：Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.title: Dazzling Lion Dance
programme.desc: Experience this ‘very Chinese time of your life’. Have you ever seen a lion that radiates a spectrum of colors? On the streets of Zhanjiang, Guangdong, an extraordinary lion dance performance is heating up the celebrations for the 2026 Chinese New Year.

programme.title: Foodwise: Quanzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in Quanzhou, the ancient starting point of the Maritime Silk Road. From its covered arcades and Roman columns to its Southeast Asian vibe, our hosts discover that Quanzhou truly is a melting pot of world cultures. programme.title: Foodwise: Xi'an
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Xi'an, an ancient city with over 3000 years of history, capital to 13 Chinese dynasties. But first, our hosts are going to carb load on street food, from glutinous rice cakes and cakes made out of persimmons, to mutton soup with flatbread and the famous biangbiang noodles. They'll also taste the rich history of Xi'an by experiencing a Qin Dynasty-inspired banquet, and try millennia-old dishes such as trout grilled on a ceramic tile and calabash chicken, a Tang Dynasty delicacy. From the Terracotta Army to the Daming Palace, residence of the Tang emperors, to a dazzling nighttime boulevard that recreates the grandeur of the Tang Dynasty, there's so much to explore in Xi'an. So, get your camera and your stomach ready for CGTN's Foodwise in Xi'an!

programme.title: Saddling up for new adventures with bold neon and traditional ink
programme.desc: This Lunar New Year, horses are set to steal the show as the Chinese zodiac migrates over to a new animal. But for one Beijing artist, born under this very sign, painting these trusty steeds is more than just a tradition – it’s an expression of freedom. Her work fuses explosive neon colors with bold ink lines. So, what drives her to create these galloping beasts?

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Why horses in British and Chinese art still speak to the Year of the Horse today
programme.desc: What does an iconic British racehorse have in common with Chinese ink paintings? Quite a lot, actually. This Year of the Horse, we’re looking at how artists across cultures have captured freedom, movement, and spirit.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. From the communal joy of folk celebrations to the enduring spirit embodied in the zodiac symbol of the horse, these showcases offer a glimpse into the profundity of Chinese heritage and wisdom, uniting the past with the present.

programme.title: Grand Song of the Dong — Natural Oriental Harmony
programme.desc: The Grand Song of the Dong is a polyphonic folk singing tradition of the Dong ethnic group. Performers from several villages gather together to sing, unaccompanied. The songs, which describe the history, beliefs, customs, and emotions of the Dong people, are an important part of their cultural identity and contribute significantly to their social cohesion. Generally sung in the Dong language, which has no written form, they are passed on orally from one generation to the next. Classified into various genres—including narrative and love songs, drinking and funeral songs—they are often accompanied by clapping, stomping, and dancing. Sung on occasions such as festivals, weddings, and funerals, the Grand Song, as a valuable part of the Dong ethnic group’s cultural heritage, reflects their wisdom and creativity, as well as their harmony with nature.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. As a keyboardist and composer in two boundary-pushing bands, NaraBara and Mola Oddity, he’s brought his unique sound to audiences in Europe and beyond. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.title: Exploring Ethnic Attire: Dong Elegance
programme.desc: Dong clothing weaves together tradition, craftsmanship, and the unique identity of the Dong ethnic group. In this episode, we’ll unravel the stories behind the intricate designs, vibrant colors, and deep cultural significance of Dong attire. From ceremonial garments to everyday wear, each piece is imbued with the essence of a rich heritage.

programme.title: Calm, Cool & Cultured: How one local jewelry designer is reimagining the Chinese zodiac horse
programme.desc: As the Year of the Horse gallops into view, a Chinese designer who was herself born in this zodiac year is putting a fresh spin on how we view this cherished beast of burden—one jewel at a time. Shen Li paid Zhang Jilin a visit to explore how she blends her vibrant energy with quiet elegance in her craft.

programme.title: Crossroads of Cultures: The Legacy of Silk Roads
programme.desc: Quanzhou, situated on the southeastern coast of China, once served as a maritime hub of the East and Southeast Asia trade network during the 10th to 14th centuries, gaining prominence for its exceptional trading port. With 22 distinctive heritage sites listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, this city stands as a testament to the legendary history of the Silk Roads. In this program, we invite four individuals living in Quanzhou to showcase their daily lives, capturing their journeys through the city's world heritage sites. Through their perspectives, we present a dynamic portrayal of a city rich in heritage. From the maritime splendor of Quanzhou's history to the serene echoes of its ancient city, from the historical treasures of the Luoyang Bridge to the vibrancy of the modern urban landscape, we journey alongside our guests through time and space, exploring Quanzhou's diverse charm and unique allure. Join us as we immerse ourselves in a city that bridges history and cultures, and embraces innovation.

programme.title: Unbridled: Graffiti artist taps animal spirit to spray city with zodiac energy
programme.desc: As the advent of the Year of the Horse brings a new kind of energy to 2026, Ma Xiao, aka. Max017 isn’t just adding kaleidoscopic colour to a local wall; he’s charging into the zodiac year of his birth with unbridled energy. By fusing ancient Chinese philosophy with the edgy aesthetics of street graffiti, he is transforming urban slabs of concrete into living tributes to the beauty of the horse—all through the nozzle of a spray can.

programme.title: The Elegance of Luoyang
programme.desc: Luoyang, as the eastern starting point of the Silk Road, is a city with a rich history and a tradition of cultural inclusivity. As such, it enjoys a prominent position in the heritage of the whole world. In this episode, we’ll visit White Horse Temple to learn about its fascinating international background. At Longmen Grottoes, which were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the year 2000, we’ll appreciate how the unique ancient splendor is being revived by 3D technology. At the city’s annual Peony Festival, we’ll explore the significance of China’s national flower and national dress. Invited to a Luoyang Water Banquet, we’ll learn something about the city’s culinary traditions. And finally, a master of tang sancai, or tri-color pottery, will discuss the legacy of this ancient craft and its place in the modern era.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Zodiac Girls’ New Year Heights
programme.desc: This zodiac year, the ancient idiom "MaDaoChengGong" promises that success will gallop right to your door. Our culture host, Julian Waghann, saddled up to meet some young equestrians whose personal quests might just teach us all how to leap into our own lucky year! Take a look.

programme.title: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River
programme.desc: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River is a documentary focusing on the World Heritage sites and cultural–ecological conservation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Through the lens of Ningxia’s heritage stories, the film highlights China’s commitment to World Heritage preservation, ecological restoration, and cultural continuity — presenting to global audiences a land where history and modernity intertwine, and where desert and oasis coexist. By following the guardians of the Western Xia Imperial Tombs, desert restorers in the Tengger Desert, Great Wall rangers at Sanguankou, traditional sheepskin raft craftsmen, and managers of the Yellow River irrigation system in Qingtongxia, the program reveals Ningxia’s distinctive contributions to cultural heritage, natural ecology, and intangible traditions — and the enduring human spirit behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise：Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: The sound of casting
programme.desc: For centuries, the fires of craftsmanship have never faded in Pingyao. In this UNESCO World Heritage city once famed for trade, three ancient metalworking traditions — sword casting, gold and silver crafting, and iron forging — continue to thrive. This episode steps into the workshops where artisans shape metal with fire and devotion. Each blade’s edge, each ornament’s gleam, and each curve of wrought iron tells a story of resilience and artistry — revealing how the spirit of Pingyao’s craftsmanship still glows in the heart of time.

programme.title: World Heritage in China: Ancient City of Pingyao
programme.desc: Established in the 14th century, Pingyao retains the typical layout of the county-level cities of the Han people in Central China. The ancient city is a complete community comprising walls, streets and lanes, shops, houses and temples.?As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Pingyao remains a testament to traditional Chinese urban planning and architecture, attracting visitors from around the world who seek to explore its historical streets and vibrant history.

programme.title: World Heritages in Handan
programme.desc: Handan, a renowned historical and cultural city in China, boasts abundant cultural and tourism resources, including the Handan Museum and Congtai Park in Congtai District, as well as the Xiangtangshan Grottoes, Guangfu Ancient City, Cizhou Kiln, etc. Handan also has a long-standing connection with the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, a world cultural heritage. As a great project created in ancient China, the Grand Canal has not only exerted a profound impact on cities along the route in terms of transportation, economy and culture, but also served as an important driving force for Handan's development.

programme.title: Kesi
programme.desc: Silk is a classic symbol of Chinese culture. It helped opened up economic and cultural exchanges between East and West and witnessed the spread of Eastern civilization to the world. As a representative of traditional Chinese silk art, kesi is renowned for its highly ornamental weaving techniques of highlighting warps and breaking wefts, and has been deeply loved by people for thousands of years. In folk culture, it enjoys the reputation of “an inch of kesi is worth an inch of gold.”

It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture. This episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Dazzling Lion Dance
programme.desc: Experience this ‘very Chinese time of your life’. Have you ever seen a lion that radiates a spectrum of colors? On the streets of Zhanjiang, Guangdong, an extraordinary lion dance performance is heating up the celebrations for the 2026 Chinese New Year.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: Boxing through the Holidays
programme.desc: Staying active during the holidays can be a challenge, especially with all the food and festivities tempting you at every turn. But what if you could sneak in a workout without having to hit the gym? Next, join Lyne Lin and Jason as they show you how to stay active during the holiday season.

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Saddling up for new adventures with bold neon and traditional ink
programme.desc: This Lunar New Year, horses are set to steal the show as the Chinese zodiac migrates over to a new animal. But for one Beijing artist, born under this very sign, painting these trusty steeds is more than just a tradition – it’s an expression of freedom. Her work fuses explosive neon colors with bold ink lines. So, what drives her to create these galloping beasts?

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Why horses in British and Chinese art still speak to the Year of the Horse today
programme.desc: What does an iconic British racehorse have in common with Chinese ink paintings? Quite a lot, actually. This Year of the Horse, we’re looking at how artists across cultures have captured freedom, movement, and spirit.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. From the communal joy of folk celebrations to the enduring spirit embodied in the zodiac symbol of the horse, these showcases offer a glimpse into the profundity of Chinese heritage and wisdom, uniting the past with the present.

programme.title: The sound of casting
programme.desc: For centuries, the fires of craftsmanship have never faded in Pingyao. In this UNESCO World Heritage city once famed for trade, three ancient metalworking traditions — sword casting, gold and silver crafting, and iron forging — continue to thrive. This episode steps into the workshops where artisans shape metal with fire and devotion. Each blade’s edge, each ornament’s gleam, and each curve of wrought iron tells a story of resilience and artistry — revealing how the spirit of Pingyao’s craftsmanship still glows in the heart of time.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. As a keyboardist and composer in two boundary-pushing bands, NaraBara and Mola Oddity, he’s brought his unique sound to audiences in Europe and beyond. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.title: World Heritage in China: Ancient City of Pingyao
programme.desc: Established in the 14th century, Pingyao retains the typical layout of the county-level cities of the Han people in Central China. The ancient city is a complete community comprising walls, streets and lanes, shops, houses and temples.?As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Pingyao remains a testament to traditional Chinese urban planning and architecture, attracting visitors from around the world who seek to explore its historical streets and vibrant history.

programme.title: Calm, Cool & Cultured: How one local jewelry designer is reimagining the Chinese zodiac horse
programme.desc: As the Year of the Horse gallops into view, a Chinese designer who was herself born in this zodiac year is putting a fresh spin on how we view this cherished beast of burden—one jewel at a time. Shen Li paid Zhang Jilin a visit to explore how she blends her vibrant energy with quiet elegance in her craft.

programme.title: World Heritages in Handan
programme.desc: Handan, a renowned historical and cultural city in China, boasts abundant cultural and tourism resources, including the Handan Museum and Congtai Park in Congtai District, as well as the Xiangtangshan Grottoes, Guangfu Ancient City, Cizhou Kiln, etc. Handan also has a long-standing connection with the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, a world cultural heritage. As a great project created in ancient China, the Grand Canal has not only exerted a profound impact on cities along the route in terms of transportation, economy and culture, but also served as an important driving force for Handan's development.

programme.title: Unbridled: Graffiti artist taps animal spirit to spray city with zodiac energy
programme.desc: As the advent of the Year of the Horse brings a new kind of energy to 2026, Ma Xiao, aka. Max017 isn’t just adding kaleidoscopic colour to a local wall; he’s charging into the zodiac year of his birth with unbridled energy. By fusing ancient Chinese philosophy with the edgy aesthetics of street graffiti, he is transforming urban slabs of concrete into living tributes to the beauty of the horse—all through the nozzle of a spray can.

programme.title: Kesi
programme.desc: Silk is a classic symbol of Chinese culture. It helped opened up economic and cultural exchanges between East and West and witnessed the spread of Eastern civilization to the world. As a representative of traditional Chinese silk art, kesi is renowned for its highly ornamental weaving techniques of highlighting warps and breaking wefts, and has been deeply loved by people for thousands of years. In folk culture, it enjoys the reputation of “an inch of kesi is worth an inch of gold.”

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Zodiac Girls’ New Year Heights
programme.desc: This zodiac year, the ancient idiom "MaDaoChengGong" promises that success will gallop right to your door. Our culture host, Julian Waghann, saddled up to meet some young equestrians whose personal quests might just teach us all how to leap into our own lucky year! Take a look.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest–tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture. This episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.desc: In "One Perfect Day in Kentucky," BFF’s Kimberly and Elsa bring their shared competitive streak to the Bluegrass State, facing off to find out who can plan the perfect Kentucky day. Each is determined to delight - and outdo - the other with unforgettable experiences that showcase the state's rich culture. Elsa kicks off the competition with a classic Kentucky breakfast, a recipe she learned from top Chef Ouita Michel at her Holly Hill Cooking Studio. Elsa wins the first point, but Kimberly’s ready to up the ante, whisking Elsa away for a thrilling cave kayaking adventure at the Gorge Underground. As they ride the chairlift to the top of the stunning Natural Bridge, the rivalry kicks into high gear and they go head-to-head in a trivia battle. The next surprise – a toast with Kentucky’s own Ale-8 soda , sourced by Kimberly straight from the factory only whets their whistles. At the Keeneland Racetrack they sip some spirit forward Keeneland Breezes while Elsa reveals all she has learned about racehorses from a visit to renowned trainer Mark Simms Jr. ‘s horse barn. A Betologist gives them a quick lesson on wagering and Kimberly’s horse wins the race. At Louisville’s Trouble Bar, Kimberly shares her newfound knowledge of Kentucky bourbon production from a tour and tasting at Castle + Key distillery and makes Elsa One Perfect Drink.

programme.title: One Perfect Day in Kentucky (2024)
programme.desc: In "One Perfect Day in Kentucky," BFF’s Kimberly and Elsa bring their shared competitive streak to the Bluegrass State, facing off to find out who can plan the perfect Kentucky day. Each is determined to delight - and outdo - the other with unforgettable experiences that showcase the state's rich culture. Elsa kicks off the competition with a classic Kentucky breakfast, a recipe she learned from top Chef Ouita Michel at her Holly Hill Cooking Studio. Elsa wins the first point, but Kimberly’s ready to up the ante, whisking Elsa away for a thrilling cave kayaking adventure at the Gorge Underground. As they ride the chairlift to the top of the stunning Natural Bridge, the rivalry kicks into high gear and they go head-to-head in a trivia battle. The next surprise – a toast with Kentucky’s own Ale-8 soda , sourced by Kimberly straight from the factory only whets their whistles. At the Keeneland Racetrack they sip some spirit forward Keeneland Breezes while Elsa reveals all she has learned about racehorses from a visit to renowned trainer Mark Simms Jr. ‘s horse barn. A Betologist gives them a quick lesson on wagering and Kimberly’s horse wins the race. At Louisville’s Trouble Bar, Kimberly shares her newfound knowledge of Kentucky bourbon production from a tour and tasting at Castle + Key distillery and makes Elsa One Perfect Drink.

Chunz and Makh set out to discover the sounds and messages of unity emerging in the African community with traditional performer Christian Adeti and dive into a new genre of Somali rap with rapper DJ Fawzi. programme.title: American Beats (2025)
programme.desc: Known as the quintessential party music, Polka is alive and evolving in the great city of Milwaukee. At the beloved festival of Germanfest, Polka Hall of Fame legend Peggy Mueller showcases her traditional roots while The November Criminals share their fusion of polka and hip-hop, making it clear there is something for everyone. From buttonboxes to beers and brats, this is a city full of personality and a deep love for its musical heritage.

programme.title: American Beats (2025)
programme.desc: Kansas City, Missouri, is an integral part of jazz history in America. Shaped by legends who once graced its streets, it is bursting with deep history, mouth-watering cuisine and a lively jazz scene. World-renowned trumpeter, tap dancer, and entertainer, Lonnie McFadden and celebrated singer and tap dancer Chloe McFadden, show Chunz and Makh what it’s all about. From finger-licking barbecue to sports events and a bustling nightlife, this city is a cultural hub offering endless opportunities for a fun-filled getaway.

programme.title: Police Patrol S1
programme.desc: De stranden van Rio de Janeiro trekken toeristen, maar achter het plaatje van een ansichtkaart gaat een hardere realiteit schuil: favela's die worden geregeerd door drugsbendes. Om deze gebieden terug te winnen, heeft de regering BOPE ingezet, een elite-politie-eenheid die sinds 2008 de strijd op straat aangaat.

programme.title: Police Patrol S1
programme.desc: Als een van 's werelds grootste cocaïneproducenten is Peru een magneet voor internationale drugskartels. Om de handel bij de bron te bestrijden, werd de elite-antidrugseenheid Sinchi opgericht, die de strijd tot diep in het hart van de productiegebieden voert.

programme.title: Police Patrol S1
programme.desc: Met een van de hoogste moordcijfers ter wereld telt Acapulco 104 moorden per 100.000 inwoners. In deze dodelijke omgeving zet een speciale anti-misdaadeenheid dagelijks hun leven op het spel om te voorkomen dat de stad in chaos vervalt.

programme.title: Police Patrol S1
programme.desc: In de multiculturele centra van Parijs en Londen kunnen de spanningen hoog oplopen. Het is aan de politie om de verschillen te overbruggen en de vrede te bewaren - dagelijks aan het werk om enkele van de drukste hoofdsteden van Europa te beschermen.

programme.title: Police Patrol S1
programme.desc: In Hyderabad, India, bestaan rijkdom en armoede naast elkaar. Elke dag strijden 15,000 agenten tegen criminaliteit variërend van diefstal tot interreligieus geweld. In Palestina staan 8,500 politieagenten voor een nog grotere uitdaging: werken in een gefragmenteerd, politiek gespannen landschap waar elke patrouille risico's met zich meebrengt.

programme.title: Police Patrol S1
programme.desc: In Catalonië heeft de regionale politie het overgenomen van de Spaanse nationale politie en een snelle-reactie-eenheid op motoren ingezet om de stedelijke criminaliteit aan te pakken. Ondertussen werkt de politie in Haifa, de belangrijkste havenstad van Israël, volgens strenge wetten in een gespannen omgeving die wordt gevormd door terrorismedreigingen en het voortdurende regionale conflicten.

programme.title: Wardens S6
programme.desc: Wachtmeester Bryan Golie van regio 4 zet de achtervolging in op jagers die een wildcontrolepost omzeilden. Een bijna vier uur durend onderzoek onthult precies wat ze verborgen hielden.

programme.title: Wardens S6
programme.desc: Wachtmeester Nick Taylor van regio 5 komt in het vizier wanneer een jager een wapen recht op hem richt. En in regio 2 ontdekken de wachters een jageres met een geheim dat ze verbergt.

programme.title: Wardens S6
programme.desc: Wachtmeesters van Regio 3 achtervolgen een loper van de controlepost en ontdekken dat de jagers een hert hebben geschoten – maar wat en waar is de vraag?

programme.title: The New Fly Fisher S16
programme.desc: Mark Melnyk vaart over de beroemde North Platte River in Wyoming, te gast bij de Ugly Bug Fly Shop. Op zoek naar grote forel met sprinkhaanimitaties!

programme.title: The New Fly Fisher S16
programme.desc: Bill Spicer verkent de rivieren van Zuid-Ontario met verschillende gidsen om bruine en regenboogforel te vangen.

programme.title: The Hunt for Monster Bass S1
programme.desc: Presentator Ott DeFoe gaat in hartje winter in Tennessee op jacht naar largemouth bass van dubbele cijfers.

programme.desc: Techknow kijkt naar innovatieve oplossingen voor toegankelijkheid en ondersteunende technologie voor mensen met een handicap.

programme.title: Extraordinary Humans S1
programme.desc: De mensen die Thom onderzoekt in deze aflevering beweren krachten te bezitten waarvan alleen gedacht wordt dat deze in het dierenrijk bestaan.

programme.title: Extraordinary Humans S1
programme.desc: Thom ontmoet een man die beweert de snelste mens op aarde te zijn en een man die een vorm van echolocatie gebruikt om te zien hoe de wereld om hem heen geluid gebruikt.

programme.title: Extraordinary Humans S1
programme.desc: Thom vindt een man die een grotere rechte- dan linkerarm heeft en geeft een andere man de ultieme opdracht: een brand blussen met het water dat hij in zijn maag heeft.

programme.title: Secrets of the Brain S1
programme.desc: Jack maakt kennis met twee mensen die steeds maar weer in slaap vallen en komt de gevolgen van slaapgebrek te weten.

programme.title: Secrets of the Brain S1
programme.desc: Jack maakt kennis met een Britse man die is ontwaakt uit een coma en nu alleen Frans spreekt.

programme.title: Combat Countdown S1
programme.desc: De capaciteit om precisiewapens in te zetten heeft de aard van oorlogvoering volledig veranderd. Vooruitgang in de wapentechnologie heeft het mogelijk gemaakt om een raket door een specifiek raam van een gebouw te schieten vanaf 1500 kilometer afstand.

programme.title: Health Explored S2
programme.desc: Reis naar het hoogste meer ter wereld om te zien wat er gebeurt in dit kwetsbare ecosysteem. We sluiten ons Bolivianenavontuur af met een ceremonie ter ere van onze planeet.

programme.title: Health Explored S2
programme.desc: Het kleine team deelt hun meest indrukwekkende momenten, verhalen, plekken en mensen, en hoe deze hun leven en gezondheid hebben veranderd.

programme.title: Heavy Metal Monsters S1
programme.desc: Een toegewijd team van ingenieurs is vastbesloten om electriciteit te geven aan de geïsoleerde gemeenschap van Slate Falls, Ontario. Daarvoor zijn ze afhankelijk van een ongelofelijk unieke machine. Deze bijzondere electriciteitspalenzetter is gemaakt van het chassis van een Hitachi 240 graafmachine!

programme.title: Heavy Metal Monsters S1
programme.desc: Wat doe je als je meer dan 160 kilometer verwijderd bent van de dichtstbijzijnde weg? Dan haal je het grote geschut erbij. En er zijn maar weinig machines groter dan de Boeing Vertol heavy lift helikopter.

programme.title: Heavy Metal Monsters S1
programme.desc: In de heuvels ten westen van St. Louis, Missouri, loopt een panter rond. De Prinoth Panther is het ultieme all-terrain, multifunctionele werkvoertuig. Het is een kraan, het is een tractor, het is een graafmachine: het is alles wat je nodig hebt.

programme.title: Space Greed S1
programme.sub-title: Sol Ownership: Can A Corporation Own The Sun?
programme.desc: De mens is altijd hebzuchtig geweest. Zeker wanneer het om de behoefte voor energie gaat. Wie weet betalen we in de toekomst abonnementskosten voor zonlicht?

programme.title: Space Greed S1
programme.sub-title: Terraforming: Can We Build A Planet B?
programme.desc: Wanner we eenmaal infrastructuur hebbben gebouwd om op gevaarlijke plekken buiten de aarde te leven, waarom zouden we dan niet verder willen ontwikkelen?

programme.title: Space Greed S1
programme.sub-title: Carbon Costs: Is Space Exploration Even Worth It?
programme.desc: Elke raket die wordt gelanceerd, heeft invloed op de atmosfeer. Kan de aarde elk jaar de honderden of zelfs duizenden lanceringen van brandstofverslindende raketten overleven?

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Europe: A Turbulent Future (2015)
programme.desc: Over time, the Atlantic Ocean widened. Then Africa moved north, struck Europe and birthed the Alps. Erosion, volcanic activity, and ice ages fashioned an extraordinarily rich and varied continent, ready for the arrival of human beings.

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Europe: Tropical Beginnings (2015)
programme.desc: One billion years ago there was just one great continent on earth. It began to break apart and Europe drifted away. Tectonic collisions, tropical vegetation, inland seas and hot lagoons are what temperate contemporary Europe is made of.

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Asia: Rising Mountains and Sinking Countries (2015)
programme.sub-title: Asia: Rising Mountains and Sinking Countries
programme.desc: Effects from the Indo-Asian collision were felt thousands of kilometers away. The deforming pressure towards the East created Indochina, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan. How else could the remains of primitive Asians have been found in Java?

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Asia: The Tectonics of Life and Death (2015)
programme.sub-title: Asia: The Tectonics of Life and Death
programme.desc: First Asia hurtled into Europe. Then, India crashed violently into the Asian continent. That shock gave birth to the highest mountain range in the world, the Himalayas. But it also released dangerous gases believed to have caused dinosaur extinction...

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Oceania: The Tectonic Ring of Fire (2015)
programme.sub-title: Oceania: The Tectonic Ring of Fire
programme.desc: Australia is now a solid and stable continent surrounded by more volatile neighbors. Pacific and Australian plates clash across the South Pacific causing intense geological and volcanic activity. Travel back in time through deserts, rock and fossils.

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: South America (2015)
programme.desc: One glance at a map of South America says it all: Andes and Amazonian basin. Two huge geological characteristics that describe how the continent came into being. The Amazon was once under the sea.

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Central America (2015)
programme.desc: Central America takes us back to when the world was young. A fragile line of islands linking North and South America, the islands of the Caribbean are recent apparitions on earth and may not be here to stay.

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: North America (2015)
programme.desc: North America's physical features were formed by volcanic eruptions, earthquakes and an ice age. To understand the geological forces at play, we look at the Rockies, the Grand Canyon and Canadian Shield. Also - will part of California become an island?

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: Africa Today (2015)
programme.desc: Volcanic activity and climate change define Africa's modern geological history. Recently meaning 50 million years ago the Arabian plate snapped off the African continent and joined Southeast Asia.

programme.title: Voyage of the Continents: The Origins of Africa (2015)
programme.desc: Africa is Mother Earth. Gondwana, the first, single, landmass broke apart into today's continents, but its heart is Africa. Land of rifts, lakes and volcanoes, Africa's mineral deposits testify to its eons-old history.

programme.title: Space: The New Frontier (2018)
programme.desc: The Japanese Asteroid Sample Return Mission has reached its target and is surveying the space rock, ready to dip down to acquire its sample. The return of asteroid material to Earth will aid scientists in the development of planetary defense systems.

programme.title: Space: The New Frontier (2018)
programme.desc: We're looking hard, but the numbers aren't stacking up. Is life on other planets really that hard to find? Does it even exist? We have not discovered so much as a signal, so maybe we really are alone in our neck of the galaxy!

programme.desc: Air, water, food, electricity and fuel all the essentials to explore the solar system, this episode explores the innovative plans for astronauts to grow their own food and extract water and fuel at their destinations.
